title: Convergent Evolution: Why Nature Keeps Inventing the Same Thing
question: Why do sharks, dolphins, and extinct ichthyosaurs — a fish, a mammal, and a reptile — all end up with nearly the same torpedo-shaped body?
summary: Unrelated lineages separated by hundreds of millions of years keep arriving at the same anatomical solutions, suggesting evolution is less a random walk than a search that keeps finding the same peaks.
